newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Some unwinding in slack trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Some unwinding in slack trade.

text.p: Investors were unwinding stock index options positions Wednesday ahead of Friday's November expiration, but participants said trading was quiet, with the underlying market under pressure.
"We've seen some positions being unwound but we've had sellers on both sides, puts and calls," said independent market maker Jack Callahan at Chicago Board Options Exchange.
He said it appeared some unwinding was taking place both in November and December S&P 100 index .OEX options.
Traders said that with the market down all morning, some investors were locking in profits as premiums declined.
But overall, activity was sluggish, they said.

"We've done some but really not as much as you would expect given what the market's doing," Hank Nothnagel, senior vice president of options trading at EVEREN Securities, said, referring to index trading.
At noon, the Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI was down about four points at 6,262. It had reached a session low of roughly 6,243.
Among broader market indices, the OEX was off half a point at 706.38 after hitting 704.58. The S&P 500 index .SPX lost a fraction to 729.38. Its session low was about 728.
Among OEX options, the most active was the November 705 call, which traded 10,330 contracts. Its open interest was about 17,000 contracts.
The corresponding put traded about 10,130 contracts. Its open interest was 18,245.
Both the November 705 call and put were down, with the call losing 5/8 to 4-3/8 and the put down 3/8 at 2-9/16.
In the December series, the busiest OEX options included the 680 put, the 705 put and call and the 715 call.
Callahan said some investors were dipping in to buy on the market's decline.
"There seems to be some waiting in the wings," he said. "We've been getting very little pullback here. Intraday (declines) has provided the best opportunities."
Trading in SPX options was extremely slow, particularly on CBOE, where the bulk of trading had shifted into the December series.
Even so, the most active options were the March 650 put, which traded 6,140 contracts and the March 670 put, which traded 4,100.
In the March 650 put, 6,000 contracts crossed in a block as a spread.
In the March 670 put, most of the volume was from spreads, mainly in blocks of 200.
In the SPX December series, most action was seen in the calls, led by the December 690, 725, 730 and 700 strikes. The most active calls included the 725, 750 and 770 strikes.
